# THEORYs with `tags` `psychopathology-and-treatment`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Psychopathology and treatment** — what a mental disorder is and how psychological treatment changes it — medical models of illness (biomedical, biopsychosocial, network), the philosophy of psychiatry, functional and transdiagnostic accounts of psychopathology such as experiential avoidance and psychological flexibility, and psychotherapies and their mechanisms of change (ADR-021).

| [THEORY-044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-044.md) v2 | Self as context is a learned deictic perspective | Barnes-Holmes et al. ([LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)) define three selves: the conceptualized self, the content of verbal relations about oneself; the knowing self, their ongoing process; and the transcendent self, their context. Hayes et al. ([LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)) say the third arises from deictic frames (I–you, here–there, now–then) as "a sense of self as a locus or perspective", and is "a context for verbal knowing, not the content", so its limits "cannot be consciously known". The account maps the three onto the record's holdings: the content is the narrative self (Dennett, Gallagher, Strawson), and the context is what Hume could not find among his perceptions and what Metzinger calls a transparent perspective. It differs from the minimal self (Gallagher) on origin: RFT says the perspective is learned in language. The evidence for the learned origin is cited, not read, so Proposed. The clinical claim is [THEORY-051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-048.md) | Biology implements psychological functions | Kendler (2008), [LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md): following Marr, a lower-level theory either replaces a higher-level construct (temperature by mean kinetic energy) or implements it, and in psychiatry biology "will implement but not replace psychology". The thesis is argued from neuroscience's successes in perception, learning and memory, not from a psychiatric case, so it is Proposed. It is a thesis about explanation, not about distinct mental causes: it survives Pernu's argument ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) that the neural evidence supports only mental causation by identity. Kendler 2005 ([LIT-552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-552.md)), which argued the mind–brain propositions this paper develops, is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-050.md) | Psychological inflexibility is transdiagnostic | Hayes et al. ([LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)) model psychopathology as inflexibility: cognitive fusion supports experiential avoidance, which narrows behaviour. Barnes-Holmes et al. ([LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)) give the mechanism: once a word stands in derived relation to an event it can carry that event's aversive functions, so private events become worth avoiding. Kashdan and Rottenberg ([LIT-553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-553.md)) find inflexibility across depression and anxiety in cognitive, behavioural and physiological systems, and say its causal role is unknown. The evidence is correlational, small, mostly self-report and mostly from the model's authors, and the meta-analysis that would test it ([LIT-543](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-543.md)) is unread, so Proposed. It is compatible with the loop account of disorder, not a rival to it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md) v4 | Self as context is how ACT reduces suffering | ACT names the self as context as one of its six processes: from it "one can be aware of ones own flow of experiences without attachment to them", so it fosters defusion and acceptance, and mindfulness exercises and metaphors foster it (Hayes et al., [LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)). RFT reads defusion as moving thoughts from I HERE NOW to I THERE THEN, a deictic shift (Barnes-Holmes et al., [LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)), labelled "no more than a heuristic". No study in the record tests the self as context as a process. Its only support is borrowed from small defusion studies under RFT's reading, so Proposed on weak grounds. The conceptual account of the self is [THEORY-044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-044.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md) v2 | Need frustration is transdiagnostic | Vansteenkiste, Ryan and Soenens (2020, [LIT-561](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-561.md)) propose that need frustration, distinct from mere lack of satisfaction, plays "a transdiagnostic role", citing a longitudinal study in which it predicted adolescents' depressive and eating symptoms and "largely accounted for their co-occurrence". Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) had located the etiology of "various forms of psychopathology" in developmental need deprivation, with need substitutes, controlled styles and rigid patterns as the route. The evidence is correlational, mostly self-report, and from the theory's authors. A partner of the inflexibility account, not a rival. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-053.md) | Efficacy is not evidence for a theory of change | Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)): "The effectiveness of a treatment is not evidence for the validity of the theory on which it is based", with one exception, that changing the theory's crucial factor without changing the problem disconfirms it. Hofmann and Hayes ([LIT-544](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-544.md)), from the other wing of CBT: a model whose process cannot be shown to apply "is incorrect and needs to be set aside" even if the intervention works, and a procedure that fails to move the process leaves the model untested. Active because it is close to a logical point and both state it. What it does not say is that mediation proves a mechanism; both sources deny that. | Active |
| [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Disorders are causal loops, not latent causes | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. Borsboom ([LIT-547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)) makes disorder an alternative stable state of a strongly connected symptom network, kept up by hysteresis after its trigger has gone. Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) make it a threat meaning protected by the behaviour it drives. Kendler ([LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)) finds causal loops across levels, from genes to culture. The convergence is real; the evidence is indirect, simulated or clinical, and none of it is an individual time series showing hysteresis, so the account is Proposed. It says nothing about what starts a disorder. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) v2 | Precise harm priors can sustain themselves | Linson, Anderson, Markham, Friston & Moutoussis (2025), [LIT-983](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-983.md), read in version 2 in [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md). A mechanism shown in illustrative simulation: policy selection by expected information gain, plus a confident prior, withholds the only disambiguating observations, so the prior keeps itself up. Exposure that restores sampling rebalances it; a precision-lowering drug only suppresses symptoms. No data are fitted, parameters are unreported, and the two intervention arms differ in environment as well as mechanism. | Active |
| [THEORY-409](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-409.md) | Mind is protective parts led by a Self | Schwartz, [LIT-579](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-579.md) (the IFS Institute's "Evolution" essay, read in [NOTE-453](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-453.md)) and [LIT-591](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-591.md) (Internal Family Systems Therapy, chapter 1 only, [NOTE-457](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-457.md), Skimmed). The model in its developer's words. Its evidence is clinical: clients' reports of parts, the founding "step back" case, and "hundreds of clients for more than two decades". No study is reported in either source, and the book's research chapter was not read. It is filed as the account IFS offers, not as an account the record has tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-560](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-560.md) | Gut–stress link strong in rodents, weak in people | Forssten et al. (2022), [LIT-915](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-915.md), read in [NOTE-703](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-703.md). A narrative review with no search method, by employees of a probiotics manufacturer, which documents its own translational failures: L. rhamnosus JB-1 had no effect on any outcome against placebo after "comprehensive preclinical evidence". The rodent half is well documented; the human half rests on one meta-analysis of healthy volunteers and trials with nulls. Proposed because the source is a narrative industry review; the gap it describes runs against its authors' interest. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-680](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-680.md) | Emotion regulation differs by point of action | Gross (1998), [LIT-554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-554.md), read in [NOTE-429](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-429.md), the founding review. It reports no data. The five families (situation selection, situation modification, attentional deployment, cognitive change, response modulation) are "working distinctions". The antecedent and response contrast rests on a handful of film studies it cites: reappraisal lowered negative experience, suppression did not reliably do so and raised sympathetic activation. The paper's own first open problem is whether regulation can be told apart from generation at all. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-892](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-892.md) v2 | Psychopathy is one dimension, not a type | Hare and Neumann (2008), read in [NOTE-1094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1094.md). The PCL-R's twenty items load on four correlated factors, which pair into Factor 1 (interpersonal, affective) and Factor 2 (lifestyle, antisocial) and are explained by one superordinate factor. The affective features are tied to the antisocial ones, so the authors deny that any component is the disorder's core, and they read the evidence as dimensional. Filed for the record's question on corporate psychopathy, which asks which of these features could be said of a corporation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-895](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-895.md) v2 | Drugs sensitize wanting, not liking | Berridge and Robinson (2016), [LIT-1461](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1461.md), read in [NOTE-1109](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1109.md) from the PMC author manuscript. A review by the theory's authors. Strong in rats and moderate in people for drugs; weak for behavioural addictions, where the authors call the evidence emerging and the mechanism unknown. Filed separately from [THEORY-893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-893.md), which holds the liking–wanting dissociation, because what [QUESTION-267](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-267.md) and [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) need is the sensitization result: a ranking whose strength is re-keyed to cues, cut loose from both pleasure and the person's goals, and lasting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-897](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-897.md) v2 | Anxiety alters learning-rate adjustment | Brown, Price & Dombrovski (2023; preprint 2022), [LIT-1479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1479.md), read in full from the NIH author manuscript in [NOTE-1120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1120.md). Their Table 2 and the synthesis drawn from it: under volatility anxious people adjust learning too little except after very surprising outcomes, and under noise they learn too fast, an effect the authors call less consistent. A narrative review of seven studies, not a meta-analysis; the reading that anxiety cannot tell noise from change is the authors'. | Active |
| [THEORY-901](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-901.md) v2 | Available avoidance blocks extinction | Mancinelli & Bach (preprint 2025; NBR 2026), [LIT-1477](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1477.md), read in full from the PsyArXiv preprint in [NOTE-1134](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1134.md). Rated A ("protection from extinction", 9 studies; "less efficient or more effortful AR imply less protection from extinction", 6 studies) in a systematic review of 116 studies. Healthy volunteers, shock or noise. The authors' explanation, that effective avoidance leaves fewer chances to detect a change, is marked "putatively". | Active |
| [THEORY-903](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-903.md) v2 | Dropping safety behaviours lowers symptoms | Goodson, Patel, Zech, Sala & Cougle (2026), [LIT-1491](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1491.md), read in full from the PMC author manuscript in [NOTE-1128](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1128.md). 26 studies reviewed, 16 in the reduction and 5 in the increase meta-analyses. The size of the safety-behaviour change moderated the symptom effect (B = 0.23). Egger's test was significant for the reduction effect on symptoms, and the increase studies could not be tested for bias. It says nothing about the mechanism by which safety behaviours act, and diagnosed anxiety disorders are thinly represented. | Active |

| [THEORY-910](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-910.md) v2 | Avoiding uncertainty perpetuates avoidance | Brown, Price & Dombrovski (2023; preprint 2022), [LIT-1479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1479.md), read in full in [NOTE-1120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1120.md). | [THEORY-1621](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1621.md) v2 | Child survivors' daughters showed no difference | Fridman (2011), a Leiden PhD thesis read in place of its promotors' meta-analyses ([NOTE-1291](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1291.md)). Small (32 survivors, 33 comparisons, 79 daughters), with selective attrition and daughters recruited for having an infant. It also restates the meta-analyses, at second hand and without effect sizes: no second- or third-generation traumatization in non-clinical samples with adequate designs. The parenting route of [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md), tested with the identity route held fixed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1627](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1627.md) v2 | Post-war family milieu outweighs wartime history | Danieli, Norris and Engdahl (2016), read in place of Danieli's 1998 handbook ([NOTE-1307](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1307.md)). A web sample, one informant for every measure, no comparison group of non-survivor families, and indirect effects of .05 to .06. It locates [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s parenting route among survivors' children without showing harm against others, and so is compatible with Fridman's null. | Active |
| [THEORY-1673](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1673.md) | Gut microbes contribute to, not cause, disorders | Almarzooqi et al., read in [NOTE-1773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1773.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of the microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA) in psychiatry, organized around the move "from association to causality". It sets out a graded hierarchy of causal evidence (confounder-controlled association, temporal precedence, experimental necessity/sufficiency, human genetic or interventional validation, cross-cohort replication), reviews mechanisms (immune, HPA, vagal/ENS, barrier), grades the evidence per disorder, and reviews translation (psychobiotics, diet, FMT, biomarkers). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1676](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1676.md) | Loot-box whales are at-risk gamblers, not rich | Secondary analysis of loot box data: Are high-spending "whales" wealthy gamers or problem gamblers? (Close, Spicer, Nicklin, Uther, J. Lloyd, H. Lloyd 2021), read in [NOTE-1784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1784.md) (Read). A secondary analysis pooling six open-access survey datasets (found through structured literature searches before 28 March 2020) with self-reported monthly loot-box spend and Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) scores, three of them also with self-reported earnings. After removing outliers (> $1000/month spend, > $250,000 earnings), 7,771 loot-box purchasers remain (5,933 with earnings). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1690](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1690.md) | Tolerance is the hub of problematic porn use | Ince et al. (2024), Problematic pornography use and novel patterns of escalating use, read in [NOTE-1726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1726.md) (Read). Two cross-sectional online samples of male pornography users (N1 = 1,356 USA; N2 = 944 UK). Measures: the five-item Brief Pornography Screener (BPS) for problematic pornography use (PPU); the PPCS tolerance subscale split into quantitative tolerance (two items, averaged) and qualitative escalation (one item); binge frequency; edging; tab-jumping. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1707](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1707.md) | Porn content escalation is multidimensional | de Roos and Willkomm, read in [NOTE-1789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1789.md) (Read). A cross-sectional online survey of 228 men aged 18–35 (mostly students, recruited through a university participant pool and social media) asked about arousal to and viewing frequency of many pornography categories, and measured sexual sensation seeking (SSS), problematic pornography use (PPCS subscales), child-sexual-abuse myth endorsement and peer acceptance of CSAM. "Escalation" is operationalized per category as viewing frequency multiplied by reverse-coded arousal: viewing a category more than one finds it arousing. A principal-component analysis finds five escalation clusters. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2209.md) | Ketamine raises approach under threat | Vestring et al. (2026), [LIT-3079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3079.md), read in [NOTE-2300](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2300.md). The nearest design of a second kind that [LEAD-047](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-047.md)'s search found: a drug intervention on the arbitration of approach and avoidance with the objective threat fixed. The represented threat is not measured. Proposed until replicated with the session order counterbalanced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2210.md) | Withholding avoidance didn't change expectancy | Sridhar, Biagi & Wake (2026), [LIT-3076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3076.md), read in [NOTE-2299](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2299.md). The nearest design [LEAD-047](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-047.md)'s search found to an intervention on what governs action with threat belief measured. Its expectancy null is clean; its avoidance effect is not. Proposed until the avoidance effect is shown confirmatorily. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2219](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2219.md) | Loot-box design features are largely unstudied | Ivern and Carbonell, read in [NOTE-2309](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2309.md) (Read). A PRISMA-ScR scoping review: 72 studies, 136 features in 22 subcategories and 6 categories, grouped by the problem they cause players and ranked by how often the literature names them. The authors find the impact and interaction of the features largely unstudied, and place the risk in interacting features within monetization systems rather than in any single one. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2241.md) | Brief mindfulness speeds responses briefly | Ge et al. (2024), [LIT-916](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-916.md), read in [NOTE-2331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2331.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In 70 students low in trait mindfulness, monitor-and-acceptance training sped conflict and inhibition responses at post-test, left accuracy and delay discounting unchanged, and had no effect at follow-up. A dissociation of speed from discounting, not a test of whether discounting mediates a change in self-control: [ARG-206](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-206.md) holds that it does not show [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)'s route. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2242](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2242.md) | Safety behaviours didn't hurt spider exposure | Meckes et al. (2025), [LIT-3123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3123.md), read in [NOTE-2332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2332.md). A randomized test of exposure held fixed with a safety behaviour cut or kept, the design [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md) names, with a null on outcome at one month. Proposed until replicated beyond one session and one small sample; it says nothing about cutting a person's own maintaining safety behaviour. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2243.md) | Threshold autoregression can detect hysteresis | de Jong et al. (2023), [LIT-3124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3124.md), read in [NOTE-2333](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2333.md). The test [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md)'s "individual data showing hysteresis" would need, with its conditions: a measured driver crossing an upper and then a lower threshold. Its depression case is simulated, and it reports no empirical psychopathology series. Proposed until its simulation results are reproduced or the paper is published as it stands. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2244](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2244.md) | Critical slowing precedes some relapses, weakly | Smit et al. (2025), [LIT-3125](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3125.md), read from its preprint in [NOTE-2334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2334.md). Within-person evidence, across 37 people, of the destabilization a tipping point predicts before entry into depression, in a minority of those who relapsed. Proposed until replicated in another sample; it is not evidence of hysteresis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2277.md) | PTSD delays first gaze to background context | Zidda, Steiger-White, Winkelmann, Ruttorf, Andoh, Nees & Flor (2025), [LIT-3174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3174.md), read in full in [NOTE-2406](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2406.md). A gaze bias against the context of a trauma cue, specific to PTSD against trauma-exposed controls, measured only as the latency of the first look, and tied to poorer relational memory. The nearest study found to the first half of [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md); it has no recall manipulation, and its background does not disambiguate. Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2280.md) | Parent depression transmits environmentally | Lewis et al. (2011), read in part ([NOTE-2370](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2370.md)). The same IVF cohort as Rice et al. 2010, used on the parenting side. It shows that the rearing route carries a parent's distress without genes or gametes, for depression symptoms. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it is the parenting route isolated from inheritance, for a non-traumatic exposure. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2284.md) | PTSD gaze lingers on trauma; rest is thin | Diotaiuti, Spica, Di Siena, Cavicchiolo, De Souza, Andrade & Mancone (2026), [LIT-3179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3179.md), read in full in [NOTE-2382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2382.md). A map of what the eye-tracking literature on PTSD has measured. For [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md) it is a check on absence: no included study measures gaze after cued recall, and the use of gaze to track engagement with corrective context in exposure is called hypothetical. The last clause of the title is the reader's count from the review's Table 1, not a sentence of the review. The corpus misses at least two eligible studies. Proposed until an independent search agrees. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2293.md) | Epigenetic trauma transmission evidence is thin | Zhou and Ryan (2023), read in full ([NOTE-2368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2368.md)). The field's own survey, by authors open to the epigenetic route, reaches the scope that [CLAIM-644](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-644.md) takes from Horsthemke: no human design yet separates germline transmission from shared genes, environment and behaviour. That corroborates [CLAIM-644](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-644.md) independently of the sceptics' school. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2297](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2297.md) | Prenatal stress effects mostly environmental | Rice et al. (2010), read in full ([NOTE-2409](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2409.md)). It is the donor-gamete design at work in humans. The design compares related and unrelated carrier–child pairs, so it splits everything the gamete carries from everything the carrying and raising mother supplies. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it shows the design that can remove the womb and rearing from a germline comparison, and the limit of that design: a gamete-borne epigenetic mark falls with the genes. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2299.md) | Hama violence linked to grandchild methylation | Mulligan et al. (2025), read in full ([NOTE-2417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2417.md)). It is the only human study found that names a germline exposure group for trauma, and it reports methylation differences there. The group is not separated from the uterine route of the middle generation, from family rearing or from the 1980 refugee community's history. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it is evidence of a difference between groups that the routes would all predict, not of one route. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's, and how much it separates is set out in [CLAIM-1017](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1017.md) and its alternative, [CLAIM-1103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1103.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2303](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2303.md) | Maltreated fathers' sperm methylation differs | Tuulari et al. (2025), read ([NOTE-2413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2413.md)). In men, a childhood exposure goes with sperm marks decades later. That is the first step of a paternal germline route, at the level of association. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it is the molecular half of a paternal design. The other half, the same men's children, with rearing removed, is missing. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2324](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2324.md) | Chatbots can co-create delusions in the vulnerable by drift | Morrin et al. (2025), [LIT-3299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3299.md), read in [NOTE-2430](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2430.md). Proposed: a perspective piece resting on 17 second-hand vignettes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2325.md) | Chatbots may fuel delusions through dissonance and opacity | Østergaard (2023), [LIT-3302](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3302.md), read in [NOTE-2428](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2428.md). Proposed: an argument by analogy with no data. On it the chatbot is the object of the delusion, a mechanism [QUESTION-548](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-548.md) did not list. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2327](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2327.md) | Feedback-optimized confirmation may fuel delusions; test it | Christensen (2025), [LIT-3283](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3283.md), read in [NOTE-2424](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2424.md), a stand-in for the unfetched [LIT-3316](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3316.md). Proposed: the account is reported second-hand, and its promote_when asks for the editorial itself. | Proposed |
